title: Driver locations: keep the latest, in memory, near the rider
brief: Design the driver-location service for a ride-hailing app. Every online driver's app sends its GPS position every 4 seconds (a write); riders see the drivers near them and matching picks the closest (a read). Each position is useful for a few seconds, then the next one replaces it.

requirements: One big city at peak: 60k online drivers x 1 update per 4 s = 15k writes/s
Only each driver's latest position matters
variants.twist: The location store dies: kill_node on it, then restore_node 10 s later. Its memory is gone. How long until the map is full again, and what does that say about making it durable? (The sim doesn't model the empty map: talk it through.)

requirements: 3 regions (us, eu, ap), one Region block each with its own client: traffic splits evenly
360k online drivers x 1 update per 4 s = 90k writes/s, plus 30k nearby-driver reads/s: 120k rps, 25% reads
A rider only ever needs drivers in their own city
variants.twist: Rush hour: most of a city's drivers sit in a few downtown cells. How do you find 'drivers within 2 km' without scanning the whole city: geohash cells, a quadtree that splits busy cells, or H3 hexagons? Which partition gets hot, and how would you split it? (The sim has no spatial index: talk it through.)

hints: A position is overwritten 4 seconds later and nobody reads the old one. Does it need a durable row on disk?

One SQL primary takes about 5k writes/s, so a row per update needs several shards. An in-memory store holding one key per driver (overwrite the latest) takes far more per node. For the global variant: does a rider in Paris ever need a driver in Tokyo?

One city: client -> LB -> about 25 services -> a Cache block used as the store (nothing behind it). Global: the same stack in each region (about 45 services), each with its own Cache block holding only that region's drivers.
_notes: One city: 20k rps = 15k writes + 5k reads. Services 1k rps each; each replica queues on its own, so near rho 1 they are slow: with a cache store, 21 services p99 ~102 ms, 22 services p99 ~54 ms (both fail the 50 ms). Naive client -> 2 services -> SQL: p99 ~5184 ms, 92% errors. A cache (hit 0.9) in front of one SQL DB doesn't help: writes pass through, p99 ~6933 ms, 87% errors. SQL sharded behind a router LB (5k writes/s per primary): 4 shards rho 1.0, p99 ~114 ms; 5 shards p99 ~36 ms but $5.06. KV (10k ops/s per node): x 2 is at rho 1.0 (22 services p99 ~80 ms, $2.83); x 3 needs 23+ services for the p99 (23: p99 ~44 ms, $3.23), over $3. A Cache block as the store, nothing behind it (50k ops/s, rho 0.4): 23 services p99 ~40 ms, $2.48; 25 services p99 ~30 ms, $2.68; 28 services $2.98; 30 services $3.18, over budget. Global: 3 regions, 40k rps each (30k writes + 10k reads); LB 50k/node, so one LB per region is enough. Naive: p99 ~5184 ms, 99% errors. 45 services per region all writing to one cache (4 replicas) in us: eu and ap pay 70 ms per call, p99 ~114 ms ($14.19). A SQL DB per region still melts (p99 ~8704 ms, 96% errors). KV x 5 per region: p99 ~50 ms but $18.09. A cache per region (rho 0.8): 43 services p99 ~70 ms (fails); 44 services p99 ~54 ms, $13.74; 45 services p99 ~45 ms, $14.04; 46 services p99 ~40 ms, $14.34; 48 services $14.94; 50 services $15.54, over $15. Not modeled: the spatial index (geohash / quadtree / H3 cell lookup for 'drivers within 2 km'), the matching algorithm, the empty store after a restart (drivers refill it within one 4 s update), and hot downtown cells. Talk them through in estimation and the twists. Checked in frontend/src/lessons/content.test.ts.
